title: An event bus
description:
Build `EventBus` for Delve.

- `subscribe(event, priority, handler)` registers a `std::function<void(long long value)>` for an event name and returns a subscription id (any number unique to this bus).
- `publish(event, value)` calls every handler for that event, **highest priority first**; handlers with equal priority run in the order they subscribed. It returns how many handlers ran.
- `unsubscribe(id)` removes a subscription and returns whether it existed. It must be safe to call **from inside a handler** during `publish`, including for the handler itself or for one that has not run yet in this dispatch (which then must not run).
- Handlers subscribed during a `publish` do not run in that same dispatch.
hints: Keep each event's handlers in a vector sorted by priority (highest first), inserting a new one after all entries of equal or higher priority.

To make dispatch safe, publish from a copy of the ids taken at the start, look each one up as you go, and skip any marked removed. `unsubscribe` only marks entries; actually erase them when no dispatch is running.
lessonTitle: Instrumenting Functions in Your Own Program
